workPackageTitle: Run scene, snapshot bridge, entity-handle lifecycle
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91-verification-strategy.md § Verification registry). This file was created in the same commit that first implements against it, and every entry below was authored before the production code it names.

'status' takes exactly one of 'registered', 'implemented', 'retired' (doc 91 § Entry status). 'evidenceKinds' is read against 'status' (doc 91 § What evidenceKinds means): for a 'registered' entry the list is evidence the verification will produce once built, and nothing may treat it as produced.

The structural validator for this file is owned by TASK-FND-009-002. Until it lands, this file is checked against tests/verification/SIM-007.json by hand, and the claim is about SHAPE only: every entry here carries the same field names with the same types - 'status' a bare string, 'scenarios', 'evidenceKinds', and 'fixtures' arrays - and the optional 'deferredTo' is absent. An earlier revision of this file rotated four of those fields against each other, so 'status' held a scenario ID in an array and 'evidenceKinds' held an artifact path, which doc 91:63 names as its own example of a value that is not a kind. It is corrected above. What is NOT yet matched is the kind vocabulary: 'engine-report', 'canonical-transcript', and 'reference-capture' are absent from doc 91 § What a kind may name's inventory, doc 91:78 requires a kind to be minted there before it may appear in a registry file, and minting those three is a correction this file still owes.

This file is deliberately NOT named SIM-0*.json. tests/MechaMiner.Simulation.Tests/Support/NegativeControlCoverageTests.cs globs 'SIM-0*.json' and asserts a totals line accounting for every entry across those seven files, so adding an entry to one of them from another work package would break an unrelated package's gate.

Every entry in this file is 'registered', and that is a structural fact about this repository rather than an omission. tests/MechaMiner.Game.Tests references MechaMiner.Content, MechaMiner.Persistence, and MechaMiner.Simulation and does NOT reference MechaMiner.Game, and build/verify-architecture.sh § 3 asserts that reference set exactly, so adding the edge would fail the accepted project boundary. No code under game/ is reachable from any test project as the boundary stands. Until that is resolved, presentation verification is an engine-tier procedure driven through a scene, not an NUnit selector.

The engine-tier procedure these entries name is game/tests/RunSliceEvidenceHarness.tscn, development scaffolding on the same footing as game/tests/GodotTestRunner.tscn: game/MechaMiner.Game.csproj removes game/tests/ from compilation under ExportRelease, so it is absent from the assembly in a Release build rather than merely filtered from an export.

The harness is not yet wired into a verb. It is run by hand and its transcript is retained as evidence; promoting these entries to 'implemented' is the work of wiring it into the engine tier alongside verify-godot-runner.sh, and that wiring is owned by the same integration owner as build/verify-gate-wiring.sh's exemption list.

Entity-handle lifecycle - the simulation-ID to presentation-handle mapping, its idempotent disposal, and a death effect outliving its authoritative entity - is the rest of PRE-001's payload. This slice renders exactly one body, the player, which needs no handle map, so those have no entry here yet.

entries.summary: The run scene consumes the two most recent committed snapshots and interpolates presentation only: the rendered body follows the authoritative pair through the mapping, and no frame writes simulation state, so disabling interpolation changes what is seen and not where the body authoritatively is.

The run scene contains no gameplay rule: the authoritative position it renders is the one the snapshot carries, the model pivot and any presentation offset never modify it, and the scene reaches player position through no path but the snapshot.

A verb a workflow invokes launches game/tests/RunSliceEvidenceHarness.tscn and observes that the harness reached managed code and wrote a fresh transcript, so that 'the harness is wired' is a checked fact rather than a call site. build/verify-run-slice.sh is added to build/verify-gate-wiring.sh's INVENTORY (the array at :409, beside the two godot gates at :418-:419) classified 'gate', and is reached from GodotImportVerb, which .github/workflows/fast.yml runs as one of its build-verb steps; that is what makes it reached under VER-FND-005-011's rule, which verify-godot-runner.sh fails because only test-main reaches it and no workflow runs test-main. THREE THINGS ARE ASSERTED, NOT ONE. (a) The gate names the scene: at 549af81 neither godot gate does - build/verify-godot.sh:64 and :80 launch bare, 'godot --headless --path' with --import then --quit-after, and reach Boot.tscn only through game/project.godot:22 run/main_scene, while build/verify-godot-runner.sh:32 names res://tests/GodotTestRunner.tscn and :185/:205 name res://tests/DeliberatelyBrokenScene.tscn. So the reachable-scene set is three and this scene is in none of them. (b) The harness reached managed code: the gate greps stdout for RunSliceEvidenceHarness.StartupLine, the exact string 'MechaMiner: run slice evidence harness ready' declared at RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:55 and printed at :71, which exists for this purpose. (c) The transcript is this run's: the gate runs with MECHAMINER_RUN_SLICE_OUTPUT set to a directory it creates empty per invocation, asserts transcript.tsv is absent before the launch and present after, and refuses a transcript it did not just cause. Without (c) a retained artifact from a developer's hand-run satisfies (b)-shaped checks forever. The harness's own exit code becomes the verb's exit class unchanged, per doc 100 § Standard command surface ('wrappers preserve the owning tool's class rather than returning success after partial work'): 0 passes, 2 is its missing-output-directory refusal at RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:77, 4 is its assertion-failure exit at :114. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ASSERT: that any particular assertion inside the harness was evaluated - that is VER-PRE-001-005 - and that the gate ran at all rather than merely being named at a reachable call site, which is VER-FND-005-010's own stated limit ('WHAT THIS ASSERTS IS REACH, NOT EXECUTION'). Execution here is evidenced separately, by the workflow's retained verb evidence under artifacts/verbs/godot-import/, which fast.yml's 'retain the verb evidence' step at :199 uploads. NEGATIVE CONTROL, on the wiring rather than the harness. EXPECTED RED, to be replaced by observed text before promotion: delete the scene argument from the gate's launch line so it launches bare, exactly as build/verify-godot.sh does, leaving a syntactically valid gate that starts Godot, reaches Boot.tscn through run/main_scene, and exits 0 with no harness involved. Expected: the gate fails naming the absent startup line and the absent transcript.tsv, and ./build.sh godot-import exits 4. This control is deliberately NOT 'delete the scene file': that breaks the environment, which doc 91 § Negative control adequacy forbids because a red is then ambiguous between the gate catching the violation and Godot failing to load a project. The absent-scene case is VER-PRE-001-007 and is asserted by diagnostic identity for that reason.

A harness assertion that fails makes the invoking verb exit non-zero, so wiring the harness in made it able to fail and not merely able to run. This is the assertion the package exists for: a harness that passes when nothing works and is now invoked by a verb is strictly worse than one nobody invokes, because it manufactures a green where there was an honest silence. RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:114 already exits 'Quit(_assertionsFailed == 0 ? 0 : 4)', so the harness half is in place at 549af81; what is unasserted is that the number reaches the verb's exit class instead of being swallowed by a pipeline, a '|| true', a subshell whose status is discarded, or a grep whose own exit code becomes the gate's. THE CONTROL PERTURBS PRODUCTION CODE, NOT THE HARNESS, so that it is a control on the conduit and on a real defect at once. EXPECTED RED, to be replaced by observed text before promotion: set MovementInputAdapter's RadialDeadzone from 0.18 to 0.30, rebuild, run ./build.sh godot-import. Expected: the transcript's deadzone-remaps-radially section carries 'FAIL deadzone-is-0.18', 'assertions_failed' is non-zero, 'outcome failed', the harness exits 4, the gate reports the failing assertion names, and the verb exits class 4. WHY 0.30 AND NOT 0.05: the assertions in that section read the samples 0.18, 0.19, 1.0 and the diagonal (0.13, 0.13), whose radial magnitude is 0.1838 - see RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:248-249, which is the sample that tells a radial deadzone from a per-axis one. 0.30 exceeds 0.1838, so it moves 'the-deadzone-is-radial-not-per-axis' as well as the constant check, and it fires inside the range the section actually samples. A perturbation to 0.19 or 0.20 would move the constant assertion only and prove nothing about the sampled range. THE CONTROL MUST BE VERIFIED TO GO RED THROUGH THE VERB, not only in the transcript. A transcript that says 'outcome failed' beside a verb that exits 0 is precisely the defect: a control that only proves a guard threw rather than that the guarded effect did not happen, and its form here is a red transcript nobody's exit code reads. So the control's acceptance criterion is the pair - ./build.sh godot-import exits 4 AND the gate's stdout names deadzone-is-0.18 - and not either alone. A forced rebuild is part of the method for the reason tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md § Why a forced rebuild is part of the method gives: assert that the sha256 of game/MechaMiner.Game.dll differs before and after, or the probe may be measuring the previous build of the perturbed file. THREE CONTROLS THAT CANNOT FAIL, RECORDED SO NOBODY REACHES FOR THEM. Each is excluded for a measured reason and not for taste, and the second is the one the next reader will reach for first. (1) A DEADZONE PERTURBATION IN game/project.godot FIRES NOTHING IN THIS HARNESS. The harness reads adapter.RadialDeadzone from code - RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:188 logs it, :191 asserts it is 0.18, :212 passes it - and its sampled cases at :222-:249 pass the literal 0.18 to MovementInputAdapter.ApplyRadialDeadzone directly. No line of this harness reads a project setting, so an [input] deadzone edit changes nothing it observes and the run stays green. That binding is the CAPTURE harness's subject, which is why the project-file injections live in VER-UI-002-005 and the code-level one lives here. (2) NO INJECTION ON ANY AXIS CAN FAIL interpolation-stays-between-the-two-committed-anchors, BECAUSE THAT ASSERTION IS TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION AND DOES NOT REACH THE PRODUCTION INTERPOLATION PATH AT ALL. The narrow statement first, because it is the one a reader checks: RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:505-506 reads "rendered.X >= from.X - Tolerance && rendered.X <= to.X + Tolerance" and never reads rendered.Y, while the leg that produces the anchors holds due east: :480 submits SubmitThroughAdapter(run, adapter, 1.0, 0.0, ref sequence) on every one of the 12 ticks, so the two anchors differ in X alone and there is no Y motion to look at even if the predicate looked. BUT ADDING A Y PREDICATE WOULD NOT FIX IT, AND THAT IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT. 'rendered' is not an output of anything under test: the harness computes it itself at :499 as "from + ((to - from) * fraction)" over the fractions declared at :497, fraction in {0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}. So the assertion compares a convex interpolant of two endpoints against those same two endpoints, which holds for every fraction in [0,1] on every axis by arithmetic, whatever the production code does. A Y predicate would be exactly as vacuous as the X one. THE VALUE ACTUALLY UNDER TEST IS NEVER ASSERTED: pivot.Position, produced by RunSceneRoot.ApplyGroundTransform(pivot, rendered, latest.PlayerFacingRadians) at :500, is only LOGGED, at :502-503, and no Check reads it. Contrast the movement section, which does assert on pivot.Position and on all three axes - :416-418 checks "Math.Abs(pivot.Position.X - authoritative.X) < 1e-5", "Math.Abs(pivot.Position.Y) < 1e-6" and "Math.Abs(pivot.Position.Z - (-authoritative.Y)) < 1e-5" - which is the shape this section's assertion is missing. AND THE BOUND IS DIRECTIONAL, so it is not merely weak but wrong in the other direction too: it assumes to.X >= from.X, so the identical predicate would go spuriously RED on a westward leg, where to.X < from.X, without any defect present. A north-axis extrapolation defect is therefore invisible, and so is a defect on any axis; the fix is not a Y term but asserting pivot.Position against an independently computed expectation. This is a live weakness in an assertion VER-PRE-001-001 already claims (PRE-001.json:32, section interpolation-is-presentation-only, whose Check is at :509-513), NOT a hypothetical: it is recorded here and deliberately NOT fixed, because strengthening an assertion inside a section another entry claims would change what that entry means without its owner, who has been told. (3) ZEROING PlayerBaseline.BaseMovementSpeedMetersPerSecond (3.0, src/MechaMiner.Simulation/Player/PlayerBaseline.cs:86) DOES NOT MOVE assertions_run. It takes the four cardinal legs red and leaves the fifth passing: the release leg at :436-:440 asserts releasing-input-stops-the-mech as "travelled < Tolerance", which a motionless mech satisfies. Every leg still evaluates, so the count stays 28 and any pin on it never moves. It is a serviceable control for the conduit assertion in this entry and worthless for VER-PRE-001-006's pin, and that difference is exactly the trap of a control that cannot fire in the range being tested.

The count of assertions the harness actually evaluated is read and asserted, so a run that reached no comparison fails rather than passes. At 549af81 the count is reported and read by nothing: RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:101 prints 'assertions_run<TAB><n>' and :114 exits on _assertionsFailed alone, so a run that evaluated 3 of 28 assertions and printed '3' passes exactly as happily as one that evaluated 28, and a run in which every section returned early before its first Check prints 'assertions_run 0', 'assertions_failed 0', 'outcome passed' and exits 0. That is the vacuous green this entry closes. THE SELECTOR IS THE GATE AND NOT A SCENE SECTION, DELIBERATELY. assertions_run is a transcript LINE (RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:101), not one of the six '## '-prefixed headings the harness emits (:123, :185, :265, :308, :359, :472). Giving this entry an engine-scene selector reading 'RunSliceEvidenceHarness.tscn § assertions_run' would enter it into the roster VER-PRE-001-006's third anchor derives from the engine-scene selectors, and that roster is asserted equal to the emitted '## ' headings in BOTH directions - so a selector naming a line rather than a section would make that anchor red by construction, permanently, and would grow the corpus's engine-scene population from the six sections that exist to seven names of which one is not a section. The honest alternative is a real '## harness-accounted-for-its-own-assertions' section emitting the count lines, with the selector pointed at it; that is a harness change, it is not in this registry-only commit, and until it lands the gate script is what this entry names. THE GATE ASSERTS THREE THINGS ABOUT THE COUNT LINE, and the second and third are what stop it being satisfied vacuously in turn. (a) The line exists: a transcript with no 'assertions_run' line is a failure and is NOT read as zero - an absent value and a zero are different findings, and collapsing them is the defect doc 91 § Negative control adequacy's third bullet and the a-failed-check-and-an-unrun-check-look-alike case both name. (b) The value parses as a non-negative integer: a non-numeric value is a failure, not coerced - the same coercion defect VER-FND-005-012 records for exit classes, where '[[ ${class} -ne 0 ]]' read FAILED, 4x and 00 all as zero. (c) The value is greater than zero AND equal to the pin, which is VER-PRE-001-006's subject; this entry owns only the existence, the parse and the non-vacuity. NEGATIVE CONTROLS, THREE, EXPECTED RED, to be replaced by observed text before promotion. (i) Non-vacuity: make RunSliceEvidenceHarness._Ready return immediately after the header lines and before RunCameraSection at :93, leaving WriteTranscript and the Quit reachable. Expected: transcript carries 'assertions_run 0', 'assertions_failed 0', 'outcome passed', the harness exits 0, and the gate fails naming a zero count against the pin. Note precisely what this control proves that no exit-code check can: the harness exits 0 and the transcript says 'passed'. Any control whose only observation is the exit code passes here. (ii) Absent line: delete the ':101' Line call. Expected: the gate fails naming an absent assertions_run line, and specifically does not report 'count is 0'. (iii) Unparseable value: emit 'assertions_run  n/a'. Expected: the gate fails naming an unparseable count. Controls (ii) and (iii) are what make (a) and (b) real rather than defensive prose; without them the gate has a branch nobody has seen taken.

The evaluated-assertion count is compared against a committed expectation, so adding or removing an assertion is a two-line change that forces someone to state the new total, and a silently shrunk assertion set fails on the count rather than sliding in on the pattern. Same shape as the content gate's items=8 at src/MechaMiner.Tools/ContentImport/verify_content.py:640, whose own header at :632 documents the weaker mode explicitly as 'items : expected number of item files (None = report, do not assert)' - a file on this branch at 61b9ade that a reader here can open. THOSE TWO LINE NUMBERS ARE ANCHORED TO 61b9ade AND NOT TO THIS ENTRY'S OTHER REF: at the merge-base 549af81 the same two lines were :603 and :595, and both moved down by 37 when this branch merged its base and picked up the narrowed abbreviation-period rule, which added 37 lines above them and took the file from 2839 lines to 2914. Every other 549af81 anchor in this entry still holds, because that merge changed verify_content.py and nothing else, and one this revision's build/verify-gate-wiring.sh INVENTORY classifies as a gate. THE PINNED NUMBER IS 28 at 549af81, and its derivation is stated so a reader can recompute it rather than trust it: 25 Check( call sites in RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs (:132, :136, :150, :155, :159, :170, :189, :223, :229, :236, :242, :249, :291, :295, :333, :338, :345, :369, :374, :438, :445, :456, :509, :514, :528), of which :438 and :445 are the mutually exclusive branches of one five-leg loop at :398 over the legs declared at :386-:393, so 23 fixed sites plus 5 loop iterations is 28. 'grep -c Check(' returns 26 because it counts the definition at :587; that off-by-one is why the derivation is written down instead of a grep being cited. Per section: camera 6, deadzone 6, facing 2, open-tick 3, movement 8, interpolation 3. THREE ANCHORS, AND THE THIRD IS THE POINT. A pin both sides of which come from the same run is blind, and so is a set-equality between two lists an author edits in one commit - doc 91 § Negative control adequacy's third bullet: 'An invariant asserting that two sets match is blind to a correlated deletion from both sides ... Such an invariant needs a third anchor that names the expected members or their count independently of either side.' Anchor 1 is the run: the transcript's assertions_run value. Anchor 2 is a committed integer in build/verify-run-slice.sh, EXPECTED_ASSERTIONS=28, which forces the total to be restated by hand. Anchors 1 and 2 alone are the blind pair: they catch a shrunk set and they do not catch a renamed, relocated or substituted assertion, and they do not catch a section dropped in the same commit that decrements the number. Anchor 3 is INDEPENDENT OF BOTH AND LIVES IN FILES THIS PACKAGE DOES NOT OWN: the gate derives the expected section roster from tests/verification/*.json, taking every entry whose selector.kind is 'engine-scene' and whose selector.value matches 'game/tests/RunSliceEvidenceHarness.tscn § <section>', and asserts set equality in both directions against the '## <section>' headings the transcript emits, requiring at least one PASS or FAIL line inside each. At 549af81 that roster is six sections from three files owned by three other packages - interpolation-is-presentation-only and presentation-holds-no-rule (PRE-001.json:32, :63), camera-shows-24-metres-vertically (PRE-002.json:31), deadzone-remaps-radially, subdeadzone-input-preserves-facing and samples-target-the-open-tick (UI-002.json:32, :63, :94) - and the harness emits exactly those six and no seventh (:123, :185, :265, :308, :359, :472). Those six are also the entire engine-scene population of the 290-entry corpus at this ref, and the nine entries this commit adds do not enlarge it: every one of them carries a script selector, so the roster anchor keeps measuring six sections against six headings. Set equality both ways matters: a transcript section no registry entry names is also red, so a section added without a registry claim cannot arrive unnoticed. This is the same construction NegativeControlCoverageTests uses and states its reason for: 'The registry's own pointers are the structured statement of coverage and this document's headings are the structured statement of what exists, so the covered set is the intersection of two things that are already machine-readable.' WHAT THE THIRD ANCHOR DOES AND DOES NOT BUY, said plainly rather than overclaimed: it is not tamper-proof, because one author can edit the harness, the pin and another package's registry in one commit. What it buys is that doing so is a diff that touches PRE-002.json or UI-002.json, which lands in another package's review, where the two-line pin bump alone would not. NEGATIVE CONTROLS, THREE, EXPECTED RED, to be replaced by observed text before promotion. (i) Silent shrink: make RunFacingSection return before its two Checks at :291 and :295 and leave everything else intact. Expected: assertions_run 26, assertions_failed 0, outcome passed, harness exit 0, and the gate red on the pin (26 against 28) AND on the roster (subdeadzone-input-preserves-facing present as a heading with no assertion line). Two anchors fire, which is the demonstration that they are separate. (ii) Correlated edit: apply (i) and also set EXPECTED_ASSERTIONS=26. Expected: anchors 1 and 2 now agree and the run is still red, on anchor 3 alone, naming the section. This is the control that proves the third anchor is load-bearing and not decoration. Without it the entry claims three anchors and has demonstrated two. (iii) Roster drift: rename the '## deadzone-remaps-radially' heading in the harness without touching UI-002.json. Expected: red naming the entry, the section it names, and the closest headings the transcript does have - reported as a rename and not as a missing control, which is the failure mode NegativeControlCoverageTests.EverySectionNamedByAnEntryExists exists for. A CONTROL THAT MUST NOT BE USED, recorded so nobody reaches for it: setting PlayerBaseline.BaseMovementSpeedMetersPerSecond to 0. It takes four cardinal legs red and leaves the fifth, the release leg at :436-:440, PASSING, because a motionless mech satisfies 'releasing-input-stops-the-mech' asserted as 'travelled < Tolerance'; assertions_run stays 28 and the pin never moves. It is a fine control for VER-PRE-001-004 and it is worthless for this entry, and the difference is exactly the trap of a control that cannot fire in the range being tested. WHAT THE PIN DOES NOT COVER: it counts assertions and does not identify them, so substituting one assertion for another inside a section keeps the count at 28 and keeps the roster satisfied, and a section that drops from 6 assertions to 5 while another gains one passes both. Closing that needs a committed golden list of the 28 assertion names compared as a set, which golden-text below is listed for and which nobody has written.

A run in which the harness never started is a failure, and it is distinguishable from a run in which it started and passed and from a run in which it started and failed. This is the third outcome, and it needs its own case because a verb newly wired to a harness reads 'no output' as nothing to complain about: a failed check and an unrun check look alike, and the wiring is the newest and likeliest-wrong part. THREE CASES, EACH WITH ITS OWN EXPECTED DIAGNOSTIC, so that a red says which one happened rather than only that something did. (a) The scene is absent: the launch names a path Godot cannot resolve. (b) The executable is absent or is not the pinned Godot: doc 100 § Standard command surface makes that exit class 3, missing or mismatched pinned environment, and NOT class 4 - a gate that returns 4 for a broken toolchain has told the reader to fix the repository when the machine is what is broken. (c) The harness is started but never reaches managed code: the scene loads and the script does not attach, or _Ready throws before RunSliceEvidenceHarness.cs:71 prints its startup line. WHY (c) IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS THE COHERENT CONTROL. doc 91 § Negative control adequacy requires a control to be a coherent violation and not a broken state: 'If the injected violation also breaks the environment, through an unparseable file, an absent binary, or a failed subprocess, a red result is ambiguous between the gate catching the violation and the gate falling over for an unrelated reason, and a green result is worse still.' Cases (a) and (b) are exactly that shape, so their reds are asserted BY DIAGNOSTIC IDENTITY - the gate must print a message naming the missing path or the version mismatch, and a bare non-zero exit is not acceptance - while (c) is the coherent injection and is the primary control. NEGATIVE CONTROLS, THREE, EXPECTED RED, to be replaced by observed text before promotion. (i) COHERENT, PRIMARY: point the gate's launch at res://tests/GodotTestRunner.tscn, a scene that exists, loads, runs and exits 0. Nothing about the environment is broken and the verb's subprocess succeeds. Expected: the gate fails naming the absent startup line 'MechaMiner: run slice evidence harness ready' and the absent transcript.tsv, and the verb exits 4. THE GUARDED EFFECT IS ASSERTED, NOT ONLY THE GUARD: the acceptance criterion includes that the output directory contains no transcript.tsv after the run, because a gate that goes red while a stale transcript sits in the directory has proved only that a guard fired. This is why VER-PRE-001-003 requires a per-invocation empty output directory: without it this control cannot distinguish 'no transcript was produced' from 'a transcript from an earlier hand-run is still there'. (ii) Absent scene: rename game/tests/RunSliceEvidenceHarness.tscn in a COPY of the game directory, never in the tree the gate is checking - a gate that edits the repository it checks is not a gate, which build/verify-gate-wiring.sh § 5 already had to learn for its godot-import control. Expected: red naming res://tests/RunSliceEvidenceHarness.tscn as unresolvable, class 4, and NOT a generic 'harness produced no output'. (iii) Absent or unpinned Godot: run the gate with PATH not containing the pinned godot. Expected: red naming the missing pinned executable and exit class 3, not 4. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ASSERT: that the gate ran at all. A gate skipped entirely produces no verdict, and nothing inside a gate can catch its own non-execution; that is the run-manifest gap FND-005.json's notes scope and defer at :23, and it is deferred here too, which is what the deferredTo field records. It is not a successor, because nothing here is retired.
